title: The Woman Who Gave Water to a Dog
text:
Among the sayings of the Prophet Muhammad collected by al-Bukhari is a short story about a woman of the Children of Israel. She was a prostitute, the kind of person respectable people looked down on.

One hot day she came upon a dog walking around and around a well. Its tongue was hanging out and it was so close to dying of thirst that it was licking the damp earth. There was no bucket, and the water lay far below.

The woman took off her leather shoe, tied it with her head scarf, and lowered it into the well. She drew up water and gave it to the dog to drink, again and again, until it had had enough.

The Prophet said that because of this act, God forgave her. In a parallel saying about a man who did the same for a thirsty dog, his companions asked whether there was really a reward for kindness to animals. He answered that there is a reward for kindness to every living creature.
lesson: Never think a small act of mercy is too small to matter, and never assume someone's reputation tells you all of who they are.
people: A woman of the Children of Israel, a thirsty dog
source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of the Prophets (hadith 3467); the parallel story of a man is in the Book of Distribution of Water
